problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix
$B=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -4 \\ 16 & 12\end{aligned}].$

examples.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $B-\lambda I\mathbin{:}$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068962/assets/fdbcc62870aefab6214b2f24f53e9bc5654e5386639d4bc328dff3769aff2b45.png)

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $\det(B-\lambda I) = 0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-0\cdot 0 & =0 \\ (\lambda -4)^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix $B$ has only one eigenvalue $\lambda=4,$ which is a double root of the characteristic equation. 

**Note:** We also say that $\lambda=4$ has an **algebraic multiplicity** of $2.$

feedback.problem:
Find all real eigenvalues of the matrix 
$Q=[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 \\ 7 & 2\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's start by writing the matrix $Q-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
Q-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 7 \\ 7 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

Now, let's find and solve the characteristic equation $det(Q-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Q-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 7 \\ 7 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-7\cdot 7 & =0 \\ 4-2\lambda -2\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-49 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-4\lambda -45 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{(-4)^{2}+4\cdot 1\cdot 45}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4\pm \sqrt{196}}{2} \\  & =\frac{4\pm 14}{2} \\  & =-5,9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =-5$ and $\lambda =9.$
